source.title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every complex polynomial of degree 3 has a polynomial square iterative root. In other words, for every complex cubic polynomial f, decide whether there always exists a complex polynomial φ such that φ(φ(z)) = f(z) for all complex z.
accepted.context_brief: Iterative roots of complex cubic polynomials

evidence.quote: In fact, even iterative roots of polynomials are not described. Even worse: we do not know whether every complex cubic polynomial has a square root.

accepted.question_text: Consider the iterative equation Σ_{j=0}^N a_j φ^j(x) = 0 on (0,∞), where φ^j denotes the j-th iterate of φ, and let c > 0 be a positive root of the characteristic polynomial Σ_{j=0}^N a_j λ^j = 0. A theorem in the paper shows that if (i) c is a simple root, (ii) there are no other positive roots, and (iii) every other root λ satisfies |λ| > c, then the only solution on a positive domain is φ(x) = cx. The open problem is whether these three conditions are actually necessary for uniqueness of the continuous or monotone solution φ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) of this iterative equation.
accepted.context_brief: Necessity of spectral conditions in linear iteration

evidence.quote: It is an open problem whether conditions (i)–(iii) are necessary for the uniqueness of the (continuous, monotonic) solution ϕ : (0,∞) → (0,∞) of (3.2).

accepted.question_text: Classify all continuous real-valued solutions φ:R→R of the functional equation φ(x + φ(x)) = φ(x)φ(x + 1). Segal's conjecture recorded in the paper asks whether the only continuous solutions are quadratic polynomials.

evidence.quote: Regarding solutions ϕ : R → R of (3.7) with k = 1: ϕ(x + ϕ(x)) = ϕ(x)ϕ(x + 1) (3.8) let us mention the paper [228] by S. L. Segal where, among others, the following conjecture is posed: The only continuous solutions ϕ : R → R of (3.8) are quadratic polynomials.

accepted.question_text: Find all continuous self-mappings φ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) that satisfy the functional equation φ(x f(φ(x))) = g(φ(x)), where f and g are the given functions appearing in equation (3.10). The paper states that this problem was posed in full generality after special power-function cases had been studied.

evidence.quote: This is the case, for instance, with the equation ϕ(xf(ϕ(x))) = g(ϕ(x)) (3.10) studied for power functions f and g by P. Kahlig, A. Matkowska and J. Matkowski in [132]. In general case, J. Matkowski (oral communication) posed the problem to find all continuous self-mappings of (0,∞) satisfying (3.10).

accepted.question_text: Find an explicit parameter q for which Schilling's problem has a nontrivial Lebesgue-integrable solution, but the related equation φ(x) = 1/2 φ(x/q − 1/2) + 1/2 φ(x/q + 1/2) has no absolutely continuous solution satisfying the boundary conditions described in the paper. The paper notes that existence of such q-values is known abstractly, but no explicit example is known.
accepted.context_brief: Explicit q for Schilling-related non-absolutely-continuous case

evidence.quote: There does not hold a converse of this theorem: there are (cf. Theorems 5.5 and 4.7) values of q such that the Schilling problem has a non-trivial Lebesgue-integrable solution but (5.4) has no absolutely continuous solution. However, no such value of q is currently known explicitly.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every function φ:N→(0,∞) satisfying Daróczy's equation φ(n) = φ(n+1) + φ(n(n+1)) for all natural numbers n must be of the form φ(n) = c/n for some constant c.
accepted.context_brief: Daróczy equation on the natural numbers

evidence.quote: The following problems were posed by Z. Dar´oczy [72]. 1. Is every solution ϕ : N → (0,∞) of (6.1) of the form ϕ(n) = c/n with a constant c?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the sequences k:N→N for which the recurrence φ(n) = φ(n+1) + φ(k(n)) admits a positive solution φ:N→(0,∞).
accepted.context_brief: Positive solvability of generalized Daróczy recurrence

evidence.quote: 2. Determine sequences k : N → N such that the equation ϕ(n) = ϕ(n + 1) + ϕ(k(n)) (6.2) has a solution ϕ : N → (0,∞).

accepted.question_text: Find a weak additional condition that forces every positive solution φ:(0,∞)→R of Daróczy's equation φ(x) = φ(x+1) + φ(x(x+1)) to have the specific form φ(x) = c/x for some real constant c.
accepted.context_brief: Weak uniqueness conditions for Daróczy equation

evidence.quote: 3. Find a weak condition under which the (positive) solution ϕ : (0,∞) → R of (6.1) is necessarily of the form ϕ(x) = c/x (6.3) with a real constant c.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether Brownian motion can be characterized by functional equations, in the same spirit that several singular or nowhere differentiable functions can be characterized as unique solutions of simultaneous functional equations.

evidence.quote: C. Sempi [230] asked whether it is possible to characterize the Brownian motion via functional equations.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all complex-valued multiplicative sequences a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1}, meaning a_{mn}=a_m a_n for all positive integers m,n, for which there exists a nontrivial continuous function φ:R→C satisfying the replicative system (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} φ((x+k)/n) = a_n φ(x) for every real x and every positive integer n.

evidence.quote: We finish this replicativity part with a problem posed by H.-H. Kairies [138] (cf. also [135]). Characterize those complex sequences a satisfying am·n = am · an for m, n ∈ N for which there exists a non-trivial continuous function ϕ : R → C such that 1/n Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} ϕ((x + k)/n) = anϕ(x) holds for all x ∈ R and n ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: Let λ assign coefficients defining the extended replicativity system discussed in the paper, and consider its solution space inside L^1(R/Z). Is the complex-linear space of all L^1(R/Z) solutions always at most two-dimensional?
accepted.context_brief: Dimension bound for extended replicativity solutions

evidence.quote: The following question was posed by L. G. Lucht [169] in connection with the above system. Assume λ : N → CN. Is it true that the C-linear space of all its solutions ϕ ∈ L1(R/Z) is at most two-dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Classify all analytic solutions in the open unit disc of the functional equation 3zφ(z^3) = 3zφ(z^6) + φ(z^2) + λφ(λz^2) + λ^2φ(λ^2 z^2), where λ = exp(2πi/3). The Berg-Meinardus conjecture stated in the paper asks whether the only analytic solutions are the Möbius-type functions φ(z) = a + bz/(1-z) with complex constants a and b.
accepted.context_brief: Berg-Meinardus conjecture and the Collatz connection

evidence.quote: It is a conjecture of L. Berg and G. Meinardus [37; Conjecture 3], [38; Conjecture 3] that functions (10.1) are the only analytic solutions of (10.2) in the open unit disc. It is interesting that this conjecture is equivalent to the positive answer to the Collatz “3n + 1 problem” [37], [38].

accepted.question_text: Given the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x), determine weak assumptions on the data f, g, and h that allow this equation to be embedded into a continuous-time family φ(F(t,x)) = G(t,x)φ(x) + H(t,x), where F, G, and H satisfy the semigroup and cocycle relations listed in the paper, match f, g, h at time t=1, and are such that every solution of the discrete-time equation also satisfies the continuous-time one.
accepted.context_brief: Embedding a linear functional equation into continuous time

evidence.quote: The following problem concerning the linear equation ϕ(f(x)) = g(x)ϕ(x) + h(x) (10.5) was posed by L. Reich [213]. He asked under what possibly weak assumptions on the given functions f, g, h we can ‘embed’ (10.5) in the equation with ‘continuous time’ argument: ϕ(F(t, x)) = G(t, x)ϕ(x) + H(t, x).

More precisely: under what assumptions on f, g, h there exist F, G, H from a suitable class of functions solving equations F(t + s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)), G(t + s, x) = G(s, x)G(t, F(s, x)), H(t + s, x) = G(t, F(s, x))H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)) and fulfilling conditions F(1, ·) = f, G(0, ·)=1, G(1, ·) = g, H(0, ·)=0, H(1, ·) = h such that every solution of (10.5) from the considered function class satisfies equation (10.6).

accepted.question_text: Characterize the self-mappings of the plane that are conjugate to a complex polynomial, separately in the three senses listed by Targonski: conjugacy under a diffeomorphism, under a homeomorphism, and under an arbitrary bijection.
accepted.context_brief: Plane maps conjugate to complex polynomials

evidence.quote: However, we would like to remaind the following problem posed by Gy. Targonski [248]: Characterize all self-mappings of the plane which are conjugated to a complex polynomial (a) under a diffeomorphism, (b) under a homeomorphism, (c) under a bijection.

accepted.question_text: Fix r ∈ N ∪ {∞} and k ∈ N, and let D_k^r be the class of C^r self-maps f:R^k→R^k with positive Jacobian determinant everywhere. Determine whether every f in D_k^r can be represented as a finite composition of squares of maps from the same class, that is, whether there exist n and φ_1,...,φ_n in D_k^r such that f = φ_1^2 ◦ ··· ◦ φ_n^2. The paper states that this is solved positively for k=1 but remains open for k>1.

evidence.quote: The problem reads as follows. Let f ∈ Dr_k. Does there exist an n ∈ N and ϕ1,... ,ϕn ∈ Dr_k such that f = ϕ2_1 ◦ ... ◦ ϕ2_n. For k = 1 this problem was solved (positively, n = 4 is enough) by M. Kuczma [149]. For k > 1 it is still open.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Some open problems concerning Siegel’s theorem can be found in the survey paper [113] by M. R. Herman.

evidence.quote: Some open problems concerning Siegel’s theorem can be found in the survey paper [113] by M. R. Herman.
Besides [21] distribution solutions of (5.1) appear also in [236] by A. Simon and P. Volkmann where such a solution is found for q = 1/4. For other problems see [214].

needs_review.question_text_raw: An answer to a similar problem for equations is not known.

evidence.quote: An answer to a similar problem for equations is not known. It would be interesting to develop also such a qualitative study for other classes of functions, e.g. differentiable ones.
